title: Logic Pro Crash Course
subtitle: 350+ Golden Nugget Tricks
tagline: No long tutorials. No fluff. Just what actually works.

pages.label: About Me
pages.title: About Me
body: I am a working producer, not a tutorial channel. Everything in this book came out of real sessions with real deadlines — the moments where I stopped, thought “there has to be a faster way to do this,” and then went and found it.

Over the years those discoveries piled up in a scratch file. Some were buried three menus deep. Some were a key command nobody mentions. Some were just a smarter order of operations. None of them were in the manual in a way that was useful mid‑session.
This book is that scratch file, cleaned up, organised, and made clickable. It is the document I wish somebody had handed me on day one.

callout.title: How to use this book
callout.text: Do not read it front to back. Jump to the section that matches what you are stuck on right now, steal the trick, and get back to the music. Every section is one click away from every page.

pages.label: Introduction
pages.title: Introduction
body: Logic Pro is enormous. That is its blessing and its curse. Almost anything you want to do is already in there — the problem is that finding it costs you the exact thing you cannot get back, which is momentum.
This is a collection of 350+ tricks, split across 19 sections, that removes that cost. Each one is short on purpose. Title, what it does, the key command. Read it in ten seconds, use it forever.
A few ground rules so nothing here trips you up:
list: Every key command shown is the Logic Pro factory default on a US keyboard. If you have remapped anything, open Key Commands with ⌥K and search the command name — the name is always given.
Where a trick lives in a menu rather than on a key, the full menu path is written out so you can find it without guessing.
Tricks marked GOLDEN NUGGET are the ones that changed how I work. If you only steal a handful, steal those.
Tricks marked VERIFY are version‑dependent and worth confirming against the exact build you are running.
Nothing here requires third‑party plugins. It is all stock Logic.

callout.title: The one habit that matters most
callout.text: Every time you catch yourself doing something with the mouse for the third time, stop and check whether it has a key command. If it does, learn it. If it does not, make one. That single habit is worth more than any individual trick in this book.

pages.label: Key Legend
pages.title: Key Legend
body: Logic’s documentation and this book both use the Mac modifier symbols. If you are coming from another DAW, this is the page to bookmark.

keys.name: Command
keys.note: The workhorse. Most destructive or structural commands.

keys.name: Shift
keys.note: Extends a selection or reverses a command.

keys.name: Return
keys.note: Sends the playhead to the start of the project.

keys.name: Space
keys.note: Play / Stop. The most used key in the program.

callout.title: Three modifier rules that explain 80% of Logic
callout.text: 1) Hold ⌥ while dragging anything and you copy it instead of moving it. 2) Hold ⌥ while clicking any control and you reset it to its default. 3) Hold ⌥ while clicking a button in a channel strip and the change applies to every channel at once. Learn these three and you can guess your way through most of the program.
